evidence: Hang Hom Street, Phố Hàng Hòm in Vietnamese, is a charming and historic thoroughfare nestled in the heart of Hanoi's Old Quarter. This rustic gem, with its moss-covered memories of the imperial capital, has been a hub of artisanal craftsmanship since the 19th century.

The unique identifying feature of the street is the multitude of paint cans, bundles of bristle brushes, and raw wooden "tráp" stacked precariously high, spilling out close to the roadside. This bustling scene is nestled amidst a maze of alleys, right next to the cramped roadway always packed with a bustling flow of people and vehicles.
